_fixture.note: SYNTHETIC — no BRAVE_API_KEY was available on 2026-09-16 (OE1 pending). The shape follows the Brave Web Search API response documentation (query{original, altered?, more_results_available} + web.results[] {title, url, description, age, page_age, language, family_friendly, profile, meta_url, extra_snippets?}). The URLs are PUBLIC record URLs of known registries whose identifiers were taken from fixtures already in this repo (openalex_works_wt1a_20260915: DOI 10.1016/j.ydbio.2007.06.022 / PMID 17651719 / PMID 19666820 / DOI 10.1007/978-3-319-51436-9_2; alliance_orthologs_wt1a_20260915: ZDB-GENE-980526-558; ensembl_homology_wt1a_20260915: ENSDARG00000031420; uniprot_wt1a_20260915: Q9PUT7; geo_gds_wt1a_20260915: GSE178751; mcp_cache raw_paper_PMC11042071_20260613: PMC11042071). Titles are bibliographic/record titles; every description, age, page_age and header value is SYNTHETIC and NOT a measurement of the live search. `description` is present in EVERY result and `extra_snippets` in one ON PURPOSE so smoke_tools_d can MEASURE that the tool OUTPUT drops them (ADR-0084 A.3). One result (en.wikipedia.org) has no meta_url on purpose (host fallback by urlparse) and one (researchgate) has a 200-char title (title cap 120 measured). researchgate and wikipedia are the two hosts the resolver cannot map to an identifier. LG1 replaces this file with a live one (live true) and smoke_tools_d prefers it.
